cards.explanation: The answer is people. Luke says the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death, "…for they feared the people." Looking for a way tells me they hadn't found one yet, friends.
The answer is the chief priests and temple officers. Verse 4 says Judas went to discuss it with them. Verse 2 says the chief priests were already looking for a way to put Jesus to death.

The answer is True. Verse 5 says the chief priests and officers "…were delighted and agreed to give him money." So the money was part of the deal, friends. It's a heavy moment, and the text doesn't dress it up.

The answer is one with no crowd around. Verse 6 says Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus "…in the absence of a crowd." He agreed to the deal and then he started watching for the right time. The text doesn't say why a crowd mattered to him, so I'll leave that open.

The answer is Peter and John. Verse 8 names both of them. Peter, one of Jesus's disciples (Luke 6:14), and John, another of Jesus's disciples (Luke 6:14), are the pair Jesus sends to make preparations for the Passover. Two names, one errand.

The answer is that he'll be carrying a jug of water. Jesus says, "…a man carrying a jug of water will meet you." That's the whole clue for Peter and John to look for, friends. Think of it as a landmark that walks.

The answer is a large upper room already furnished. Jesus says the owner "…will show you a large upper room, already furnished." Then He tells Peter and John, "Make preparations there." Large, upstairs and furnished, all in one verse.
The answer is False. Luke 22:13 says Peter and John went and found it "…just as Jesus had told them." Then they prepared the Passover. Everything matched what Jesus said, friends.

The answer is before His suffering. Jesus says, "I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering." He's the one who wants this meal, and He says it out loud. I think that's worth leaning in close for, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes." He's not promising to keep drinking it Passover after Passover, friends. He points ahead to the kingdom of God coming.

The answer is His body given for them. Jesus picks up the bread, gives thanks, breaks it and passes it to His apostles. He says it is His body, given for them. Then He asks them to keep doing this to remember Him.
The answer is remember. Jesus says, "do this in remembrance of Me." It's an invitation to remember Him, friends. Simple words, and I'd write them on every cookie box if I could.

The answer is the new covenant in His blood poured out for them. Jesus says, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you." He says it after supper, with the cup in His hands. It's a big sentence, so read it slowly, bakers.
The answer is False. Luke 22:21 has Jesus say, "Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table." So the betrayer isn't far away, friends. He's at the table with them. It's a heavy moment.

The answer is False. Luke 22:23 says they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this. I think that means it wasn't plain to them right away, friends. The text doesn't say more than that.
